Top-level `site_name:` in app.yaml (the scaffold writes it) is the app's display name: `og:site_name` on server-rendered pages, the name in the PWA manifest, the name in the framework's sign-in emails and the issuer an authenticator app shows. `seo.site_name` wins when both are set.

The description is `seo.description`: the meta description and `og:description` of server-rendered pages (a page's own `description` setting wins) and the manifest's description. A top-level `description:` has no effect.

`frontend:` has no effect and is not reported (many apps carry `frontend.stack: html`, a label nothing reads): which stack serves a path follows the files, static/ is the TSX stack and a root *.html file is a server-rendered page (api({at:'ssr'}) files). `database:` has no effect: an app has one database. `head:` has no effect: tags for the <head> of every server-rendered page go in a `head.html` file at the app root, and a page under static/ writes its own <head>.

An app.yaml key that has no effect is accepted, so an app that carries one still pushes and deploys. A write of app.yaml (write_file, edit_file, `benmore push`, `benmore deploy`) and `benmore check` answer with one warning for each such key, which says what to write instead where something takes its place (for `description:`, `Use seo.description instead`). The keys: top-level `description`, `database`, `head`, `radius`, `shadow` and `nav` (api({at:'ssr'}) appearance), and `auth.public_api` and `auth.billing_publishable_key_env`.
